filename: Machine Learning for Clouds and Climate.pdf
title: Machine Learning for Clouds and Climate
parameterization_target: convection, cloud microphysics, radiative transfer, subgrid turbulence
testbed_rationale: This paper is a review and introductory chapter/monograph surveying machine learning tools and applications for clouds and climate; it does not produce or provide access to a new benchmark dataset.
pain_points: Key climate variables cannot be directly observed (cloud condensation rates, subgrid radiative effects), confining attempts to model emulation
Lack of labeled ground truth climate datasets for benchmarking
Extrapolation and out-of-distribution generalization under climate change / unseen regimes
Violation of physical conservation laws (mass, energy) by unconstrained ML models
Instabilities when ML parameterizations are coupled back into climate host models (online stability)
Spatial and temporal autocorrelation making train/val/test splits challenging
Underestimation of extremes in statistical downscaling / super-resolution
HPC and software infrastructure barriers for multi-node GPU/TPU scaling with dynamical cores
extraction_notes: Submitted manuscript to Geophysical Monograph Series. Represents a review chapter summarizing existing works (such as Rasp et al. 2018, Mooers et al. 2020, WeatherBench, etc.) rather than introducing a single primary dataset.
